To check what a file *contains*, read it with **`Get File`** and assert on the
string with `Should Contain`. There is no `File Should Contain` keyword — this
is a common newcomer trap. To produce a file, **`Create File`** writes content.
Write into `${OUTPUT_DIR}`, the run's output folder — a safe place that won't
clutter your workspace.

## Task 1 — Read a log file and write a summary

**Goal:** create `checks/readwrite.robot` that reads a bundled file with
`Get File`, asserts on its contents, writes a file with `Create File`, and reads
it back to confirm.

Here is the same read-then-write flow over a different file. Adapt it.

<!-- example -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library    OperatingSystem

*** Test Cases ***
Copy A Value Into A Note
    ${orders}=    Get File    sample_data/orders.csv
    Should Contain    ${orders}    travel-mug
    Create File    ${OUTPUT_DIR}/note.txt    reviewed
    ${note}=    Get File    ${OUTPUT_DIR}/note.txt
    Should Contain    ${note}    reviewed
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** the suite defines `Read And Write File Content`.

<!-- hint -->
Read the log with `${log}=    Get File    sample_data/app.log`, then
`Should Contain    ${log}    ERROR` — the log has error lines in it.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
Write with `Create File    ${OUTPUT_DIR}/summary.txt    checked`, then read it
back with `Get File` and `Should Contain    ${written}    checked`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library    OperatingSystem

*** Test Cases ***
Read And Write File Content
    ${log}=    Get File    sample_data/app.log
    Should Contain    ${log}    ERROR
    Create File    ${OUTPUT_DIR}/summary.txt    checked
    ${written}=    Get File    ${OUTPUT_DIR}/summary.txt
    Should Contain    ${written}    checked
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Run it green

Run:

```bash
uv run robot checks
```

**Check:** the log is read and the summary file is written and verified.
